name: Mugga Lane landfill
notes: Opened in the 1970s; about 1 Mt/yr received with ~70% recovered, so ~300 kt/yr landfilled. Existing 4.24 MW gas-to-energy plant makes ~37,000 MWh/yr, which this model implies is ~40% of generated methane. PROXY: constant 300 kt/yr since 1975 and closure in 2035 are assumptions; k and L0 are screening defaults. Coordinates approximate.
sources: ACT City Services, Mugga Lane Gas-to-Energy factsheet (Aug 2025): https://www.cityservices.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1653393/Mugga-Lane-Gas-to-Energy-factsheet-August2025-acc.pdf
ABC News, 20 Nov 2023, landfill gas expansion (~300,000 t/yr to ACT landfills): https://www.abc.net.au/news/2023-11-20/energy-generated-from-landfill-gas-to-power-canberra-homes/103124726

name: Lucas Heights landfill
notes: 890,134 t received in 2024 (approved up to 970,000 t/yr); waste receipt must cease at the end of 2037. Landfill gas already collected and converted to electricity by Energy Developments. PROXY: opening year 1987, tonnage before 2024 and 50% existing capture are assumptions to verify. Coordinates approximate.
sources: Cleanaway, Lucas Heights Landfill Annual Environmental Management Report 2024 (SSD-6835): https://cleanaway2stor.blob.core.windows.net/cleanaway2-blob-container/2025/03/AEMR-SSD-6835-2024-Lucas-Heights-Landfill.pdf

name: Melbourne Regional Landfill, Ravenhall
notes: Cleanaway's largest site, over 200 ha, processing over 2 Mt/yr; landfill gas is already used for electricity or renewable gas. PROXY: 2 Mt/yr since 2004, closure in 2040 and 50% existing capture are assumptions; not all tonnage processed is necessarily landfilled. Coordinates approximate.
sources: Cleanaway, Ravenhall (Melbourne Regional Landfill) site page: https://www.cleanaway.com.au/location/ravenhall

name: Redvale landfill, Auckland
notes: Opened 1993; takes about 600,000 t/yr (around half of Auckland's waste); consent ends December 2028, with an extension to 2036 proposed. Operator reports about 95% of methane captured and used for electricity (about 9 MW of engines). PROXY: constant tonnage since 1993 (operator range 600,000-800,000 t/yr); 95% capture is an operator claim; k and L0 are NZ ETS default-composition values, not site measurements.
sources: NZ Herald, Redvale extension (opening 1993, ~600,000 t/yr, 95% capture, closure 2028 extended to 2036): https://www.nzherald.co.nz/business/landfill-proposal-aucklands-biggest-landfill-set-to-stay-open-for-seven-to-eight-years-longer-than-expected-after-delays-for-new-facility/KPBOPWAYUFAKTAEYY553PFXZGQ/

k and L0: waste-weighted from NZ ETS Schedule 3 default composition, as reproduced in MfE Landfill Gas Capture Management final report: https://environment.govt.nz/assets/publications/Waste/landfill-gas-management-final-report-.pdf

name: Kate Valley landfill, Canterbury
notes: Opened 2005; received 332,000 t in 2019/20; consented to 2040. 4.3 MW of gas engines commissioned in 2014; operator reports about 96% of methane captured. PROXY: constant 330 kt/yr; 96% capture is an operator claim; k and L0 are NZ ETS default-composition values, not site measurements.
sources: Transwaste Canterbury, Kate Valley (350,000 t/yr, 2005 opening, four 1 MW generators): https://transwastecanterbury.co.nz/kate-valley/
Transwaste Canterbury 2020 annual report (321,000 t in 2018/19, 332,000 t in 2019/20): https://transwastecanterbury.co.nz/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/TCL-2020-Annual-Report-FINAL-240920_signed.pdf

name: Naboro landfill, Suva
notes: Fiji's main landfill, on the Queens Road about 24 km from central Suva, opened 2005 and serving the Suva area. A 2016 USP study found an average of 70,000 t/yr received and no methane recovery, biogas use or flaring, and estimated about 800 m3/h of methane generated in 2016; no later capture project has been found. k = 0.17 is the IPCC 2019 default for bulk waste in tropical wet climates; with it the model gives about 690 m3/h in 2016, close to the study. PROXY: constant 70 kt/yr (a 2020 report gives 184 t/day to 100 kt/yr) and the 70-year design life to 2075 are assumptions. Coordinates approximate. No Australian credit scheme applies.
sources: Mani, Maata, Gronert, Harvey and Chand (2016), Landfill gas generation and methane recovery at Naboro landfill, Fiji Islands: https://repository.usp.ac.fj/id/eprint/9188/
Fiji Sun, 28 Jul 2020, The Naboro landfill story (opened Oct 2005, 70-year design life, 184 t/day): https://fijisun.com.fj/news/investigations/the-naboro-landfill-story-every-14-months-a-new-pit
HG Leach (Fiji), Naboro Landfill (location on Queens Road ~24 km from central Suva, operating since July 2005): https://www.leachltd.co.nz/hg-leach-fiji-ltd-naboro-landfill/
